creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Calling c.Text() on a List-declared section reports:

    case.go:88: snapshots/cli/basic.snap: case "greets a name": section "ARGS"
    is declared List; use List("ARGS") instead of Text

The line the reader needs is in their own test file. They get ours.

fail() calls t.Helper(), but frame-skipping only works if every function in the
chain is marked, so the walk stops at the first unmarked frame out - Text itself.
Every misuse path lands this way: wrong accessor, undeclared section, output set
on the wrong scope.

This is the one place the library breaks its own promise that a failure carries
path:line to the spot you edit. Everywhere else it holds.

Fix: mark Has, Text, List, Out, OutInt on Case, Out/OutInt on Step, and
mustInput/mustOutput. Guard the nil case - a Case from ParseFile has no *testing.T,
so an unguarded t.Helper() would panic on the happy path for exactly the tooling
audience ParseFile exists to serve. fail() already guards it; reuse that shape.
title: Accessor misuse errors point into go-snap instead of the test file
